column2: The completion of the Lord's house, king's house and every desired undertaking introduces the second appearance, preserving the three-part scope.
Second time and the comparison with the Gibeon appearance remain; no new location is inferred here.
Propose you built for you did build as ordinary natural address without an added emphatic auxiliary. Hearing prayer, doing all requested, consecration, enduring name, eyes and heart remain.
The condition includes walking as David, holiness of heart, uprightness, doing all commanded him and keeping ordinances and commandments.
column3: Him retains the selected command's David referent, not silently changed to you.

column2: Establishing the throne for ever is tied to the condition and quoted promise of a continuing ruler in Israel; no unconditional guarantee is created.
The warning shifts to plural addressees and their children, emphatic turning, failing to keep what Moses set before them, other-god service and prostration.
column3: English you is number-neutral; the plural scope is explicit in this record and the coordinated children, without changing the preceding singular condition.

column2: Removal from given land, casting away the consecrated house and Israel becoming a disappearance and talk among all peoples remain.
column3: Disappearance for aphanismos remains a difficult provisional noun; devastation, obliteration and disappearance require further lexical evaluation rather than substitution from a parallel.

column2: The lofty house, passing through it, astonishment, hissing and question about both land and house preserve the selected description.
column3: Lofty is not converted to a heap of ruins; the location implied by through remains open.

column2: The answer names abandonment of the exodus God, slavery-house liberation, grasping foreign gods, worship and service as reasons for the calamity.
The additional notice moves Pharaoh's daughter to his house built for himself; her house is not substituted to harmonize another notice.
Twenty years and both houses introduce the Hiram assistance statement continuing in verse 11.
Cedar, pine, gold and all desired assistance precede the king's gift of twenty Galilean cities, retaining number and location.
Hiram travels from Tyre to Galilee, sees the cities and is not pleased; no stated defect is supplied.
The question, brother address and Boundary name lasting to this day remain; Cabul is not substituted for the selected translated name.
Hiram's one hundred twenty gold talents lead directly into the ship clause at verse 26 across the selected numbering gap.
The ship, Solomon's work concerning it, Ezion-geber by Elath, farthest sea and Edom remain in the inherited cross-unit syntax.
column3: The relation of and a ship to Hiram's preceding gift and hyper hou remains unresolved; a fleet independently built by Solomon is not silently substituted.

column2: Hiram's attendant sailors know how to ply the sea and go with Solomon's attendants, retaining the joint crew.
Sophira and one hundred twenty talents of gold remain selected; Ophir spelling and 420 or 450 talents are not imposed.
The queen hears both Solomon's name and the Lord's name and comes to test with riddles; the two names are not collapsed into a single reputation phrase.
Very great retinue, laden camels, spices, abundant gold and precious stones precede speaking all in her heart.
Solomon explains every matter, with the negative no-overlooked-matter clause retained rather than an added omniscience claim.
All discernment and the built house begin the queen's observed inventory, continuing into the next unit.
Food, attendants' seating, ministers' station, his clothing, wine-pourers and burnt offering precede her being beside herself.
column3: His clothing retains the selected singular possessive; the burnt offering is not replaced by a staircase or ascent.

column2: She affirms the report heard in her land about his word and discernment, preserving both subjects of the report.

Propose what they reported to me is not half of it to make the report-versus-experienced-abundance comparison intelligible. Her prior disbelief, arrival, seeing eyes, behold and added goods beyond every report remain.
column3: What they reported and of it supply the comparison's ellipsis from the following abundance claim. The close working draft retains the more literal ambiguous half clause; the Greek comparison's exact syntax remains open.

column2: Blessed women and blessed constantly attending servants remain, with all discernment; women is not replaced by men.
The queen blesses the Lord for delight, throne placement, love for Israel, enduring establishment and righteous judgment.
column3: The final in their judgments is retained as difficult selected wording; no smoother independent legal formula replaces it.

column2: One hundred twenty talents, abundant spices and precious stones remain, with the superlative spice comparison.
column3: Never again is the inherited interpretation of eti with the past-perfect arrival form; whether the emphasis is prior or subsequent unmatched supply remains unresolved.

column2: Hiram's ship from Souphir brings gold, very much unhewn wood and precious stones, preserving the different source name-form from Sophira.
The unhewn wood becomes supports and instruments for singers, with no such wood seen to this day.
column3: No special botanical species replaces unhewn; harp and lyre are provisional instrument equivalents and the unworked-to-worked description is not harmonized.

column2: All desired and requested gifts are distinguished from prior royal gifts, followed by the queen and every attendant returning to her land.
The annual gold weight is six hundred sixty-six talents, retained without symbolism or modern currency conversion.
Subject-peoples' tribute, merchants, all kings beyond and land satraps remain additional to the stated annual weight.
Three hundred hammered-gold spears and three hundred gold pieces per spear preserve the selected object and figures, not two hundred shields.
column3: Pieces supplies a generic nominal equivalent for chrysoi without assigning an unstated coin standard.

column2: Three hundred hammered-gold shields with three minas each are placed in the Forest of Lebanon house, preserving their distinction from spears.
The great ivory throne is covered with tested gold; no unexpressed purity percentage is assigned.
Six steps, calf foreparts at the rear, seat arms and two adjacent lions remain; a rounded back is not substituted for calves.
Twelve lions on the six steps, on both sides, and the no-equivalent-in-any-kingdom statement retain scope and count.
Gold drinking vessels and basins, gold-encased Forest-house utensils and unvalued silver preserve each inventory and rationale clause.
column3: Encased is the inherited contextual rendering of the gold descriptor, not an assertion of a modern plating technique.

column2: The Tarshish ship with Hiram's ships returns every three years carrying gold, silver and engraved and hewn stones.
column3: Stones are not replaced by ivory, apes or peacocks from another text; the exact workmanship of toreutos remains provisional.

column2: The full added undertaking/spoil account retains both houses, city wall, citadel, enclosure, five named cities and chariot/horsemen cities, ending with the negative rule clause continued in 22b.
column3: The relation of spoil, building program and so that there might not rule over him is unresolved. The retained cross-unit construction is provisional, not an accepted reconstruction of the infinitive's subject and autou.

column2: All seven remaining peoples, their non-Israelite status, descendants, inability to destroy and subjection to tribute remain in the additional account.
column3: The opening any of the people follows the provisional negative clause from 22a; no subject change is claimed as settled. Tribute's labor implication requires contextual review.

column2: The negative assignment of Israelites to labor contrasts with their roles as warriors, attendants, chariot commanders and horsemen.
column3: This statement is not reconciled with the earlier Israelite levy; the scope of labor/pragmatic service remains provisional.

column2: Solomon exceeds all earth's kings in wealth and discernment, retaining both grounds of comparison.
All kings seek his presence to hear discernment given by the Lord in his heart, preserving divine source and named audience.
Each annual gift list retains gold vessels, clothing, stacte, spices, horses and mules; silver or weapons are not imported.
column3: Stacte remains the selected aromatic term without a specific modern botanical identification.

column2: Four thousand mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen remain; the feminine them is clarified as mares at the two storage locations.
column3: Four thousand is not harmonized with forty thousand in chapter 2, and mares are not changed to stalls or chariots.

column2: The additional rule notice extends from the River to foreigners' land and Egypt's borders, retaining every boundary.
Both gold and silver are as stones, with cedars as plentiful lowland sycamores; gold is not dropped to match a shorter account.
Egypt and Thekoue are distinct sources, and the merchants' repeated Thekoue and exchange remain.
column3: Thekoue's geographical identification and exact exchange mechanism remain open; Kue is not silently substituted.

column2: A chariot costs one hundred silver pieces and a horse fifty; sea export goes to Hittite and Syrian kings.
column3: The selected prices and by-sea phrase remain despite their difference from familiar figures and mediation wording; no precise silver weight unit is supplied.
